The study investigates how the decay widths of baryons belonging to the exotic eikosiheptaplet depend on the number of colors, \(N_c\). In particular, it focuses on the behavior of these widths when \(N_c\) is treated as a variable rather than being fixed at its physical value of three. This type of analysis is important because the large-\(N_c\) limit provides a useful theoretical tool for understanding the structure and interactions of baryons in quantum chromodynamics.

The analysis is carried out within the framework of the Chiral Quark Soliton Model. In this approach, baryons are described as collective rotational excitations of a soliton formed by chiral meson fields. The model is especially useful for studying baryon multiplets and their properties, including masses, decay constants, and decay widths. By applying this framework, the study derives expressions for the decay widths of members of the exotic eikosiheptaplet and analyzes how these expressions scale with \(N_c\).

A central aspect of the work is its focus on exotic baryon representations that go beyond the regular baryon multiplets. Regular baryons are usually associated with familiar representations such as the octet and decuplet for \(N_c = 3\). However, in soliton-based and large-\(N_c\) approaches, additional representations can appear, including exotic multiplets that contain states not describable as simple three-quark configurations. The eikosiheptaplet is one such exotic representation, and its study provides insight into the possible spectrum and decay behavior of nonstandard baryonic states.

The text also discusses how ordinary baryon representations can be generalized to arbitrary values of \(N_c\). Since the familiar \(SU(3)\) flavor multiplets are defined most directly for \(N_c = 3\), extending them to general \(N_c\) requires a careful prescription. This generalization allows one to track how known baryon multiplets evolve in the large-\(N_c\) limit and to compare them consistently with exotic representations. By combining this representation-theoretic analysis with the Chiral Quark Soliton Model, the study provides a systematic description of both regular and exotic baryons as functions of \(N_c\), with particular emphasis on the decay properties of the exotic eikosiheptaplet.

This study investigates the large-\(N_c\) behavior of exotic baryons belonging to the eikosiheptaplet, or 27-dimensional representation, within the framework of the Chiral Quark Soliton Model. In particular, it focuses on how the decay widths of these exotic states scale with the number of colors \(N_c\), a question that is central to understanding whether such baryons remain narrow or become broad in the large-\(N_c\) limit. The analysis treats the 27-plet as a genuine exotic extension of the familiar baryon spectrum and examines its strong decays into lower baryon multiplets accompanied by pseudoscalar mesons.

A key part of the work is the extension of baryon flavor representations from the physical case \(N_c=3\) to arbitrary \(N_c\). In large-\(N_c\) QCD, the usual SU(3) representations such as the octet and decuplet do not remain fixed in the same form; instead, they must be embedded into larger \(N_c\)-dependent representations that reduce to the familiar multiplets when \(N_c=3\). The study therefore constructs the appropriate generalizations of both ordinary and exotic baryon multiplets, allowing a consistent comparison of their properties as \(N_c\) is varied.

Within this generalized representation scheme, the paper analyzes the mass splittings, transition operators, SU(3) Clebsch–Gordan coefficients, and phase-space factors relevant to baryon decays. Special attention is paid to how these ingredients combine in the large-\(N_c\) limit. The decay widths are not determined by a single factor alone: they depend simultaneously on the scaling of the axial couplings, the group-theoretical matrix elements, and the available decay momentum. As a result, the large-\(N_c\) behavior of exotic baryon widths can differ significantly from naive expectations.

The study clarifies the distinction between ordinary baryons, such as those belonging to the generalized octet and decuplet, and exotic baryons, such as the generalized antidecuplet and eikosiheptaplet. Ordinary baryons fit naturally into the large-\(N_c\) spin-flavor structure, while exotic multiplets contain states that cannot be built from \(N_c\) valence quarks alone without additional quark-antiquark degrees of freedom. This difference is reflected in their representation structure and in the way their decay amplitudes behave as \(N_c\) becomes large.

Overall, the work provides a systematic large-\(N_c\) treatment of the exotic 27-plet baryons in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model. It shows that a consistent interpretation of exotic baryon decay widths requires using the correct \(N_c\)-dependent SU(3) representations rather than simply extrapolating the \(N_c=3\) multiplets. By doing so, the study helps clarify the behavior of both exotic and non-exotic baryons in large-\(N_c\) QCD and contributes to the broader understanding of how soliton models describe baryon spectroscopy beyond the ordinary octet and decuplet.

In theoretical physics, the words **chiral**, **quark**, and **soliton** often appear together in models that try to describe the internal structure of matter.

A **quark** is one of the fundamental building blocks of particles such as protons and neutrons. Quarks interact through the strong force, which is described by quantum chromodynamics, or QCD. One important feature of QCD is **chiral symmetry**, a symmetry related to the handedness, or chirality, of particles. In the world of very light quarks, this symmetry plays a major role in explaining why certain particles behave the way they do.

A **soliton** is a stable, localized wave-like object that keeps its shape while moving. Solitons appear in many areas of physics, from water waves to field theory. In nuclear and particle physics, soliton models can be used to represent particles as stable configurations of fields rather than as simple point-like objects.

The **chiral quark soliton model** combines these ideas. It describes baryons, such as protons and neutrons, as soliton-like configurations of chiral fields interacting with quarks. In this picture, quarks move in a self-consistent background field, and the collective behavior of the system forms a stable particle. This approach provides insight into properties such as mass, spin, magnetic moments, and the distribution of quarks inside nucleons.

Although it is not the only way to study hadrons, the chiral quark soliton model is valuable because it connects the fundamental quark structure of matter with the larger-scale field patterns that emerge from strong interactions. It shows how complex particles can arise from both elementary constituents and collective phenomena.

Particular attention is paid to the embedding of baryon multiplets in arbitrary-\(N_c\) representations of flavor \(SU(3)\), which is essential for a consistent large-\(N_c\) analysis. Using collective-coordinate quantization, we derive the relevant decay amplitudes and examine how representation-dependent Clebsch–Gordan coefficients, phase space, and axial coupling constants scale with \(N_c\). We show that the large-\(N_c\) behavior of the widths is sensitive to the choice of the generalized baryon representations and to cancellations among leading contributions to the decay operators. The results clarify the status of exotic baryon decays in the soliton picture and provide a systematic framework for comparing the physical \(N_c=3\) eikosiheptaplet with its arbitrary-\(N_c\) continuation.

In large-\(N_c\) analyses of SU(3) baryons, the “ordinary” \(N_c=3\) multiplets must be embedded into \(N_c\)-dependent representations rather than kept fixed. The standard generalization is

\[
8 \;\to\; (p,q)=\left(1,\frac{N_c-1}{2}\right),
\qquad
10 \;\to\; \left(3,\frac{N_c-3}{2}\right),
\]

which reduce to the familiar octet and decuplet at \(N_c=3\). Exotic multiplets are generalized similarly; for example, the exotic eikosiheptaplet, i.e. the SU(3) \(27\)-plet, is commonly embedded as

\[
27 \;\to\; \left(2,\frac{N_c+1}{2}\right),
\]

for the \(J=3/2\) exotic tower, again giving \((2,2)\) at \(N_c=3\).

The \(N_c\) dependence of decay widths is sensitive to this embedding. For nonexotic decuplet-to-octet decays, the mass splittings and phase space shrink with \(N_c\), leading to parametrically suppressed widths in the large-\(N_c\) limit. By contrast, decays of exotic multiplets such as the eikosiheptaplet generally have mass splittings of order \(N_c^0\), so their phase space does not vanish. After using the proper \(N_c\)-dependent SU(3) representations and the large-\(N_c\) scaling of the axial couplings, the exotic \(27\)-plet decay widths are generically of order

\[
\Gamma_{27} \sim N_c^0,
\]

up to channel-dependent Clebsch–Gordan factors or possible accidental cancellations. Thus, unlike ordinary baryon resonances, exotic eikosiheptaplet states are not expected to become parametrically narrow solely from large-\(N_c\) counting.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

Collective quantization of the soliton yields a tower of flavor \(SU(3)\) representations whose rotational energies and symmetry-breaking splittings exhibit characteristic \(N_c\) scaling. We analyze how the exoticness of the eikosiheptaplet affects its mass separation from nonexotic multiplets and discuss the implications for decay amplitudes and widths. In particular, while exotic rotational excitations remain parametrically distinct from ordinary baryons, cancellations among axial couplings can modify the naive large-\(N_c\) expectations for their strong decays. These results clarify the status of higher exotic multiplets in soliton-based descriptions of baryon spectroscopy and provide a framework for assessing their phenomenological viability.
